event_name: Solution of the Robbins problem by EQP

sources.title: Robbins Algebras Are Boolean
sources.publisher_or_host: University of New Mexico mirror of William McCune's Argonne research materials
evidence_supported: EQP found the proof that solved the Robbins problem on 1996-10-10.
The successful search took about eight days on an RS/6000 processor and used about 30 megabytes of memory.
The EQP proof was used to guide Otter to a proof object that was checked by a separate proof checker.
Input, proof, proof-object, prover, and checker materials were publicly preserved.

sources.title: Solution of the Robbins Problem
evidence_supported: The peer-reviewed article presents the automated solution and the search strategies that enabled EQP to find it.
The article appeared in volume 19, issue 3 of the Journal of Automated Reasoning in 1997.
Publication followed the October 1996 machine-discovery event.

sources.title: Solution of the Robbins Problem — associated proof materials
evidence_supported: EQP and Otter inputs, proofs, and proof objects corresponding to the journal article were preserved.
The preserved materials distinguish proof discovery from later proof-object checking and journal publication.

technology_dependency.rationale: The decisive proof was found automatically by EQP; this source-expansion record preserves that dependency evidence without adjudicating the controlled seed classification.

verification_method.seed_value: Automated theorem prover generated a proof; simplified proofs followed
verification_method.clarification: EQP discovered the proof; Otter generated a proof object guided by the EQP result; a separate checker checked that proof object.

remaining_questions: Establish the exact date on which the Otter proof object and separate checker completed verification.
